FRST 100.title: Sustainable Forests
FRST 100.description: An overview of forests and forestry. Survey of the disciplines, areas of study, and values that frame sustainable management of forests in BC and the world. Assignments focus on critical thinking and written communication skills.

FRST 101.title: Principles of Microeconomics for Forestry and Land and Food Systems
FRST 101.description: Principles of microeconomics and their applications in forestry and land and food systems. The basic concept of the economy to focus on private and social decision making related to the use of land, especially in agriculture, forestry, and conservation.

FRST 107.title: Introduction to Forestry Co-op
FRST 107.description: An introduction to Forestry Co-op including: completion of preemployment workshops, career skills toolkits, networking opportunities, interview training, individual coaching sessions, and job search skills. Restricted to students meeting the requirements of the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship Co-operative Education Program. Pass/fail.

FRST 110.title: Land One: First-year Integrative Seminar
FRST 110.description: Current issues and cases in Forestry and Land and Food Systems are examined with a focus on integration of first-year subjects and exposure to both First Nations and Western perspectives.

FRST 150.title: Scholarly Writing and Argumentation in Forestry
FRST 150.description: Communicating concepts of forestry and links to human and environmental activities through writing, elements of argumentation, evaluating evidence, and searching for and citing references to back up claims; small-class experience.

FRST 200.title: Forest Plant Biology I
FRST 200.description: The structure, diversity and development of trees and other plants, with emphasis on the angiosperms.

FRST 201.title: Forest Ecology
FRST 201.description: The structure and function of forest ecosystems, including: energetics; productivity; nutrient, carbon and water cycling; soils; the physical environment; population and community ecology; disturbance ecology; ecological succession; biological diversity and ecological resilience.

FRST 202.title: Forest Ecology
FRST 202.description: The Ecosystem concept; energy biomass and nutrient cycling; the physical environment; population and community ecology; succession, Biogeoclimatic classification and some coastal ecosystems. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 203.title: Silvics of Forest Trees of Western Canada
FRST 203.description: Ecological and silvical characteristics of forest trees; assessment of ecological site quality and biogeoclimatic classification; application of silvics in silviculture. A plant herbarium of at least 50 species is required. Only available through Distance Education.

FRST 210.title: Forest Plant Biology II
FRST 210.description: The functional biology of trees and other forest plants in their environment, with an emphasis on gymnosperms.

FRST 211.title: Forest Classification and Silvics
FRST 211.description: Forest classification and the application of silvics in forest management, including world forest classification systems, the Biogeoclimactic Ecosystem Classification system, and ecosystem diagnosis in the field.

FRST 231.title: Introduction to Biometrics
FRST 231.description: Basic theories of probability and statistics. Sampling distribution, methods of estimation and hypothesis testing; goodness of fit and tests for independence; analysis of variance, regression and correlation. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:
FRST 231.corequisiteText: One of MATH 100, MATH 180, MATH 184, MATH 190

FRST 232.title: Computer Applications in Forestry
FRST 232.description: Techniques involved in solving forestry problems with microcomputers using word processing, spreadsheet, procedural language, and database management tools.

FRST 239.title: Tree and Stand Level Measurements
FRST 239.description: An introduction to measurement of individual trees and stands; use of aerial photographs, maps, and various measurement instruments.
FRST 239.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 231, NRES 231 and one of FRST 232, NRES 232

FRST 248.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 248.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Orientation workshops required. Final work term report required.

FRST 302.title: Forest Genetics
FRST 302.description: Population genetics and conservation of genetic resources; principles of genetics and their application to forestry.

FRST 303.title: Into the Woods: An Introduction to Forest Science
FRST 303.description: Introduction to growth of trees and forests with emphasis on evolutionary, ecological and environmental aspects. Not available for credit to undergraduate students in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship.

FRST 304.title: Forest Stewardship in a Changing Climate
FRST 304.description: Forests can provide natural solutions to climate change and social well-being through innovative management and restoration including protection of mother trees and soils, carbon and conservation financing, and emergence of value-added industries. For students without strong science backgrounds. Not available for credit to Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship students.

FRST 305.title: Silviculture
FRST 305.description: Silviculture concepts and principles; stand dynamics; artificial and natural regeneration; cultural techniques for forest stand establishment and stand tending; silvicultural systems; decision making and development of prescriptions; connections to forest planning.
FRST 305.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 201, NRES 201 and one of FRST 350, FRST 351, UFOR 400

FRST 307.title: Biotic Disturbances
FRST 307.description: Concepts of disturbance ecology with special reference to insects and diseases in the forests of British Columbia; forest health problems in the biogeoclImatic zones of BC; present management strategies and future potentials in a scenario of climate change.
FRST 307.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211

FRST 308.title: Forest Entomology
FRST 308.description: An introduction to insects that cause damage to forests and forest products; how insects live; life cycles and attack symptoms of representatives of major groups of insects; principles for control and management. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 309.title: Forest Pathology
FRST 309.description: Biology and management of forest tree diseases. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 310.title: Soil Biology
FRST 310.description: The diversity and interactions of soil organisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi, animals, plants) in natural and managed ecosystems; roles in primary production, nutrient cycling, decomposition and reclamation; responses to environmental change.

FRST 311.title: Plant Physiology I
FRST 311.description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants. CHEM 203, CHEM 213, or CHEM 233 and CHEM 235 is recommended.

FRST 318.title: Forest and Conservation Economics
FRST 318.description: Practical problem solving of economic issues related to forestry and conservation, touching on investment analysis, capital budgeting, non-timber economics, ecosystem services, and forest certification. Completion of FRST_V 232 or NRES_V 232 or intermediate knowledge of MS Excel essential.

FRST 319.title: Principles of Forestry Economics
FRST 319.description: Introduction to the economics of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services produced by, and dependent on, the forest resource. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 320.title: Abiotic Disturbances: Fire and Climate
FRST 320.description: Ecological effects of fire and climatic (wind, temperature, and snow) disturbances; fire danger rating, principles of fire management and prescribed fire use; windthrow risk modelling and management.
FRST 320.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 210, NRES 210 and one of FRST 211, NRES 211

FRST 339.title: Forest Level Measurement and Productivity
FRST 339.description: Obtaining and forecasting information for stands and forests.

FRST 346.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 346.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 347.title: Co-operative Work Placement
FRST 347.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 348.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 348.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 350.title: Foundational Field School
FRST 350.description: Field study concentrating on outdoor skills, forest measurements, site diagnosis, and an integrated overview of the ecological, social and economic basis for forest management. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses.
FRST 350.prerequisiteText: FRST_V 211 or NRES_V 211; FRST_V 201 or NRES_V 201

FRST 351.title: Interior Field School
FRST 351.description: Field study at an interior BC location concentrating on land use, management and silviculture. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses. Students with FRST_V 351 and FRST_V 350 can only count 3 credits toward their program requirements.

FRST 370.title: Community Forests and Community Forestry
FRST 370.description: Community forests and community forestry throughout the world, with special attention to participation by aboriginal peoples; emphasis is on forms of governance, public participation, and adaptive learning.

FRST 385.title: Watershed Hydrology
FRST 385.description: Measurement and analysis of hydrological processes in response to forest management activities.

FRST 386.title: Aquatic Ecosystems and Fish in Forested Watersheds
FRST 386.description: Effects of forest management activities on fish and aquatic ecosystems.

prerequisite.raw: Third- or fourth-year standing in Forestry, Science, Applied Science or Applied Biology

FRST 386.prerequisiteText: Third- or fourth-year standing in Forestry, Science, Applied Science or Applied Biology

FRST 395.title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
FRST 395.description: Ecology, management, and conservation of terrestrial vertebrate wildlife, focusing primarily on socio-economically important, forest-dwelling species of mammals, birds, amphibians and reptiles.

FRST 399.title: Introduction to Research Methods
FRST 399.description: Lectures and seminars in research philosophies and the scientific method, with special emphasis on field research.
FRST 399.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 150, LFS 150, NRES 150, WRDS 150, ENGL 110, ENGL 111, WOOD 225, NRES 225

FRST 402.title: Living Language: Science and Society
FRST 402.description: Multi-disciplinary course in which students, individually and in groups, examine, integrate and apply subject-specific knowledge through the lens of language and the framework of the language sciences, with a focus on themes of real-world importance.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor

FRST 402.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing or permission of the instructor

FRST 403.title: The Sustainability of Production in Managed Forest Ecosystems
FRST 403.description: Study of the functional and dynamic characteristics of forest ecosystems and their response to forest management using ecosystem-level microcomputer simulation models.

FRST 404.title: Advances in Silviculture
FRST 404.description: Fundamental silvicultural problems; the application of research findings to the practice of silviculture.

FRST 406.title: Advanced Forest Pathology
FRST 406.description: Hereditary, physiological, anatomical, environmental, and microbiological factors influencing forest tree diseases. Given in alternate years.

FRST 408.title: Advanced Forest Insect Ecology
FRST 408.description: Role of climate and climate change in the population dynamics, outbreak potentials and resultant impacts to forest ecosystems associated with herbivorous forest insects.

FRST 410.title: Introduction to Landscape Ecology and Management
FRST 410.description: Current concepts, methods, and applications of landscape ecology with emphasis on spatial patterning, spatial heterogeneity, and dynamics; problem-solving approaches to natural resource issues through the application of landscape ecological principles and tools.

FRST 411.title: Complex Adaptive Systems, Global Change Science, and Ecology Sustainability
FRST 411.description: Concepts of complex adaptive systems (CAS); exploration of how CAS can be used to manage natural and social environments for multiple goals under changing climatic and socio-economic conditions.

FRST 413.title: Ecological Plant Biochemistry.
FRST 413.description: The structure, biosynthesis, distribution and biological function of secondary plant metabolites.
FRST 413.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of BIOL 200, BIOL 201 and one of BIOL 209, BIOL 210; or (b) one of FRST 200, NRES 200 and one of FRST 210, NRES 210

FRST 415.title: Sustainable Forest Policy
FRST 415.description: The development, implementation, and analysis of forest policy.

FRST 421.title: Quantitative Forest Management
FRST 421.description: Introduction to the quantitative tools necessary in forest management. Available only through Distance Education.

FRST 422.title: Mathematical Modelling in Forest Resource Analysis
FRST 422.description: Modelling techniques used in strategic and tactical forest resources analyses.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth-year standing in the BSF degree

FRST 422.prerequisiteText: Fourth-year standing in the BSF degree

FRST 423.title: Forest Management Planning
FRST 423.description: Forest management designs to identify and integrate economic, social, and environmental objectives across a forested landscape both strategically and tactically.

FRST 425.title: Forest Planning
FRST 425.description: Analyze and interpret existing management plans, prescribe solutions for achieving specific forest management goals at multiple scales, use basic tools to evaluate the financial implications of such solutions, and create a forest management plan for a virtual forest. Offered entirely online. Students in any of the Forestry programs requiring FRST 423 (6 cr) in order to graduate will not be granted the 3 cr of FRST 425 toward degree completion.

FRST 430.title: Advanced Biometrics
FRST 430.description: Analysis of variance, multiple regression and analysis of covariance. Design and analysis of experiments.

children.raw: equivalent. Restricted to students with 4th year standing or by permission of instructor

FRST 430.prerequisiteText: One of FRST 231, NRES 231, BIOL 300, STAT 200. And FRST 399 or equivalent. Restricted to students with 4th year standing or by permission of instructor

FRST 432.title: Ecological Genomics
FRST 432.description: The genomic basis of adaptation to environments. Topics progress through community structure, life history patterns, stress responses, and variation and adaptation.

FRST 436.title: Growth and Yield
FRST 436.description: Techniques of growth and yield projection and discussion of modelling approaches. Exploration of stand dynamics, quantitative implications of management treatments and environmental limitations to tree and stand growth.

FRST 439.title: International Forestry
FRST 439.description: The socio-economic, biological and technological aspects of forestry within the international frame, in both the developed and developing world. Regional studies and the role of national and international agencies.

FRST 443.title: Remote Sensing for Ecosystem Management
FRST 443.description: Basic biological concepts related to interpretation of remote sensing data for land management, including the use of films and filters, and interpretation of air photographs, and other imagery.

FRST 444.title: Agroforestry
FRST 444.description: Ecological, economic and social benefits of incorporating trees into agricultural landscapes. Lectures and groupwork designing agroforestry systems in temperate and tropical contexts.

FRST 446.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 446.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 447.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 447.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 448.title: Co-operative Work Placement.
FRST 448.description: Supervised work experience in an approved organization for a minimum of 15 weeks. Restricted to students in the Co-operative Education Program in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship. Final work term report required.

FRST 449.title: Directed Studies in Forestry
FRST 449.description: In special cases and with the approval of the instructor concerned, a student may carry on directed studies of specific problems in forestry.

FRST 452.title: Coastal Field School
FRST 452.description: Site diagnosis and preparation of management options in coastal forests. Extrasessional course; fees will be assessed to meet expenses.

children.raw: Third- or fourth-year standing in the B.S.F. program, or Forest Management major or Forest Operations major in B.Sc. in Natural Resources program

FRST 452.prerequisiteText: FRST_V 350 or 351; FRST_V 305; Third- or fourth-year standing in the B.S.F. program, or Forest Management major or Forest Operations major in B.Sc. in Natural Resources program

FRST 456.title: The Role of Natural and Planted Forests in the Global Bioeconomy
FRST 456.description: (Go Global Seminar Series) An intensive one-month field school in Chile focused on fast-growing industrial forest plantations, innovative wood products, land use strategies for natural and planted forests, and their impact on society.

FRST 470.title: Forests and Society
FRST 470.description: Social aspects of forestry and forest communities.

FRST 475.title: Indigenous Ecologies
FRST 475.description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes.
FRST 475.prerequisiteText: One of BEST_V 203, BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, APBI_V 260, GEOS_V 207. And third-year standing

FRST 485.title: Forest Watershed Management
FRST 485.description: Effects of land management on quality, quantity and timing of water flow.

FRST 490.title: Visual Resource Management and Planning for Aesthetics
FRST 490.description: Methodologies for visual analysis, perceptions, planning & management of urban, natural and working landscapes, and implications for sustainable land-use management & community engagement.

FRST 491.title: Visualization and Forest Design
FRST 491.description: GIS-based spatial planning and 3D landscape visualization for forest management.

FRST 492.title: Environmental Perception
FRST 492.description: How individuals perceive their environment. Emphasis will be given visual perception in the context of natural resource issues and the effects of those perceptions on individuals including issues of human wellbeing.

FRST 495.title: Biological Diversity and Conservation
FRST 495.description: Principles, problems, and practices of managing natural habitats for biological diversity; current issues in biological diversity important to researchers, policymakers, and the general public. .
FRST 495.prerequisiteText: One of FRST_V 201, NRES_V 201 and FRST_V 395

FRST 497.title: Communications and Professionalism
FRST 497.description: Preparing professional reports and presentations; professionalism and professional ethics.

FRST 498.title: B.Sc. Thesis in Forestry
FRST 498.description: An independent study or research project of a subject of special interest to the student under the direction of a staff member. Available only to students in the BSFS Honours specialization.

FRST 499.title: B.S.F. Thesis
FRST 499.description: An independent study or research project on an approved topic, developed under the guidance of a Faculty member. Available only to students in their graduating year.

FRST 500.title: Teaching and Learning in Forestry
FRST 500.description: An evidence-based examination of teaching and learning in forestry, focusing on instructional design, classroom practices and field instruction.

FRST 502.title: Tropical Rainforests: Evolution, Biology, Ecology
FRST 502.description: Evolution and current structure, functions and diversity of moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the humid tropics.

FRST 503.title: Plant Molecular Biology Laboratory
FRST 503.description: Techniques of purification, cloning, sequencing, restriction-hybridization analysis of plant nucleic acids, in-vitro labeling of plant nucleic acids and proteins, and electrophoresis and immunodetection of plant proteins. Offered by the Biotechnology Teaching Laboratory in cooperation with the Department of Forest and Conservation Sciences. Admission to the course is limited and requires recommendation from the department head.

FRST 506.title: Advanced Forest Pathology
FRST 506.description: Hereditary, physiological, anatomical, environmental, and microbiological factors influencing forest tree diseases.

FRST 508.title: Advanced Forest Insect Ecology
FRST 508.description: Role of climate and climate change in the population dynamics, outbreak potentials and resultant impacts to forest ecosystems associated with herbivorous forest insects.

FRST 509.title: Advanced Biometrics
FRST 509.description: Linear model theory and application for observational data and randomized experiments. Multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of covariance. Design and analysis of experiments.
FRST 509.prerequisiteText: One of FRST_V 231, NRES_V 231, BIOL_V 300, or STAT_V 200

FRST 512.title: Belowground Forest Ecosystems
FRST 512.description: Review of current literature on specific topics in forest soil ecology, including bacterial endophytes, microbial diversity, nutrient cycling, and mycorrhizae. Students with either APBI_V 412 or CONS_V 412 will not be allowed to take FRST_V 512.

FRST 513.title: Biotechnology in Tree Improvement
FRST 513.description: Advanced research topics and their application to forest genetics. Emphasis on molecular genetics and experimental protocols.
FRST 513.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 335 or permission of the instructor

FRST 515.title: Climate Change Communications and Engagement
FRST 515.description: Psychological, social, and systemic dimensions of climate change communication; approaches for engaging diverse groups for low-carbon futures; overcoming climate inaction.

FRST 516.title: Tree Physiology
FRST 516.description: Growth and development of woody plants; physiological responses to abiotic and biotic environmental factors; consequences of silvicultural practices on physiological processes.

FRST 517.title: Economics of Forest Management
FRST 517.description: Applying economics to forest and forestland management, including analysis of how government policies and market designs affect forest management outcomes.

FRST 518.title: Land, Extraction, and The Corporation
FRST 518.description: Political ecology of resource extraction. History of the extractive corporate form. Theories of land ownership, access, and sovereignty in relation to market forces. Tensions between society, state, and the market. Global approaches to governing extraction.

FRST 519.title: Forests and Society
FRST 519.description: Emphasis on tropical and sub-tropical countries, where the majority of forest-dependent people live.

FRST 520.title: Land and Forest Resource Economics
FRST 520.description: Applications of advanced theory and quantitative analysis to problems in forest resource and land economics; multiple land use; institutions for sustainable land use; optimal management and policy.

FRST 524.title: Environmental Perception
FRST 524.description: Perceptual processes mediating behaviour in humans, with special attention given to the emotional processing of visual stimuli.

FRST 527.title: People and Forests: An International Perspective
FRST 527.description: Biodiversity loss, deforestation, desertification, salinization, air pollution and climate change facing world forests.

FRST 528.title: Social Science Research Methods for Forestry and Conservation

FRST 530.title: Advanced Modelling Methods for Natural Resources Applications
FRST 530.description: Linear, nonlinear, and generalized linear models, including mixed effects versions of each. Examples include applications to forests and other natural environments.

FRST 531.title: Multivariate Statistical Methods
FRST 531.description: Multivariate analysis of variance, cluster, principal components, factor, canonical and discriminant analysis. Theory and conceptual background are presented but emphasis is on selection of appropriate analysis and interpretation of results. Examples from forestry and related fields are analysed by computer programs at UBC.

FRST 533.title: Problems in Statistical Methods
FRST 533.description: Directed studies in problems of advanced statistical techniques as a tool in forest research.

FRST 535.title: Global Environmental Issues and Forests
FRST 535.description: Socio-economic, biological, and technological problems affecting forests and forest-dependent communities.

FRST 536.title: Advanced Studies in Forest Mensuration
FRST 536.description: Development and analysis of forest inventory systems; sequence and patterns of tree growth; analysis of crown development; improvement of stand growth and yield; methods of biomass analysis.

FRST 538.title: Advanced Geomatics for Natural Resource Management
FRST 538.description: Advanced geospatial technologies are examined and applied to pressing management issues.

FRST 540.title: Application of Operational Research Methods in Forest Management
FRST 540.description: Use of operational research methods in forest planning models; emphasis on algorithms, problem formulation and interpretation of results.

FRST 543.title: International Forestry Institutions, Diplomacy and Negotiation

FRST 544.title: Technical Communication Skills I
FRST 544.description: Principles and practice of oral presentations.

FRST 545.title: Technical Communication Skills II
FRST 545.description: Theory and practice of technical communication necessary for preparation of effective scientific reports, reviews, grant proposals, journal articles and theses.

FRST 546.title: Research Methods and Philosophies in Science
FRST 546.description: Lectures and seminars in research philosophies and methods with special emphasis on field and applied research.

FRST 551.title: Landscape Planning for Sustainability
FRST 551.description: Analysis, perception, planning of landscapes, and integration of social acceptability with sustainability.

FRST 552.title: Tropical Forests: Management and Conservation
FRST 552.description: The use, management, and conservation of tropical and sub-tropical forests.

FRST 554.title: Forest Products and Services
FRST 554.description: Global trends in products and services.

FRST 555.title: Fundamentals of Sustainable Forest Land Management
FRST 555.description: Concepts and principles at the site and landscape scale.

FRST 556.title: Land Information Acquisition and Analysis
FRST 556.description: Principles and application of data acquisition and use.

FRST 557.title: Site-Level Forest Land Management
FRST 557.description: Design and implementation of site-level plans that integrate ecological, social, and economic components: silviculture, forest operations, and forest health.

FRST 558.title: Landscape-Level Forest Land Management
FRST 558.description: Preparation of landscape-level sustainable forest management plans that integrate ecological, social, and economic components.

FRST 561.title: Quantitative Methods in Wildlife Ecology
FRST 561.description: Concepts and applications of statistical methods for common questions in the ecology, conservation, and monitoring of animal populations.

FRST 562.title: Topics in International Forestry
FRST 562.description: Contemporary and emerging issues in international forestry.

FRST 575.title: Indigenous Ecologies
FRST 575.description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes.

prerequisite.raw: A second-year or higher ecology course

FRST 575.prerequisiteText: A second-year or higher ecology course

FRST 578.title: Directed Studies in Forest Business and Management

FRST 580.title: Topics in Forest Business and Management

FRST 588.title: Fluvial Ecohydrology
FRST 588.description: Hydrology, geomorphology and ecology of streams and their catchments; significance of stream processes within the fluvial network; management issues, particularly in the context of forest harvesting.

FRST 593.title: Climate Adaptation in Socio-Ecological Systems
FRST 593.description: Theory and evolution of adaptation at different scales in organizations and resource management systems, utilizing existing case studies, examining opportunities and barriers to adaptation, considering strategies and practices to manage climate impacts and risks.

FRST 595.title: Transformative Environmental Research
FRST 595.description: Scholarly foundations of and emerging approaches for engaging creatively and critically in environmental research that recognizes (and potentially addresses) issues of power, difference, and complexity, transforming both the researcher and the research discipline.
